text.p: Orange Plc, Britain's youngest mobile phone operator, said on Tuesday that its customer base had topped 850,000 at the end of February.
At the end of December, subscribers to its digital network had risen a sharp 107 percent to 785,000.
Orange, which reported its first annual results since flotation last March, said its market share had risen to 11.5 percent from seven percent.

The company noted that its churn rate -- a measure of the proportion of customers disconnecting from the network or being excluded for bad debt or fraud -- was the lowest of the UK's four mobile operator rivals at 18.6 percent, up from 18.1 percent in 1995..
Reporting its first annual results since flotation last March, Orange said it had managed to sustain the key annual revenue per subscriber at 442 pounds.

'Our average retained revenue per customer of 442 stg a year is now the highest in the industry, while our churn rate of 18.6 percent remains by far the lowest,' said managing director Hans Snook in the results statement.
'Low churn and higher average revenues mean we are building a more valuable customer base with significantly higher estimated contributions per customer than the industry average,' he added.
Orange earlier reported annual pre-tax losses of 229 million pounds against 141 million in 1996. Analysts, who had expected losses to come in at 223.3 to 237 million stg.
Heavy investment needed as it builds out its network means that the company is not expected to become profitable before around 1999.
